candidate_relations.reason: Septic emboli may contribute to infarcts but do not capture KP invasive syndrome with liver, lung, kidney, brain, infarcts, and pneumocephalus.
Blood, liver, and pleural cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, not Bacteroides fragilis.
Klebsiella pneumoniae infection names the organism but omits invasive syndrome, multi-organ sites, infarcts, and pneumocephalus.
Emphysematous pyelonephritis captures renal gas but not liver, lung, brain, infarcts, or pneumocephalus.
Severe hyperglycemia with acidosis is a precipitant/comorbidity, not the invasive Klebsiella syndrome.
Describes the brain complication only, missing KPIS and other organs.
Endogenous endophthalmitis is a classic KPIS site but no ocular findings are recorded, so this organ scope conflicts with the documented composite.
Cultures are Klebsiella pneumoniae, not Staphylococcus.
Cerebral gas gangrene implies clostridial myonecrosis-type infection, incompatible with documented KP and pneumocephalus.
Klebsiella sepsis is a parent of invasive syndrome but lacks specified liver/lung/kidney/brain involvement, infarcts, and pneumocephalus.
Cerebral gas embolism is a related intracranial-gas mechanism distinct from infection-associated pneumocephalus in KPIS.

case_quality_flags: No candidate encodes the full KPIS multi-organ infarct and pneumocephalus composite
